newsitem.title: UK: Europe split on single currency-poll.
newsitem.headline: Europe split on single currency-poll.

text.p: The British have turned sharply against the European Union while the vast majority of Germans want a referendum on a single currency, according to a major new poll conducted across the continent.
Voters in Germany, Britain, France and Italy were asked idential questions about the planned Euro currency and the future shape of the European Union.

The British proved to be the least enthusiastic, according to the results published in the Friday edition of the Daily Telegraph. Only 42 percent say they would vote to stay in the EU if there was a referendum while 38 percent would vote to leave.
Seventy percent of Germans said they wanted to have a referendum on a single currency. For Britain the figure was 76 percent.
Italy emerged as the biggest supporter of the European Union with 82 percent backing continued EU membership and 71 percent favouring a single currency.
Only one quarter of Britons said they would vote in favour of a single currency compared to more than 60 percent in France and more than 70 percent in Italy, the poll showed.
